A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Action Motifs/A4Mer paper, with 24 readable pages including Appendices A–C. Pages 2–24 have identical text and rendered content; page 1 differs only in its project link and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original action-recognition, motion-prediction, and motion-interpolation experiments, component ablations, hyperparameter analyses, and evaluation of foot-camera-assisted pose annotation.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results in Sections 4–5 and the appendices, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: A4Mer's two-stage architecture, Action Atom/Motif segmentation, masked latent prediction, loss decomposition, and downstream procedures are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use AMD and Humans in Kitchens for the same recognition, prediction, and interpolation tasks. The appendix evaluation with HiK's original multi-label annotations is also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. Table 2 and the corresponding appendix comparisons retain MotionBERT, USDRL, PUMPS, MacDiff, BehaveMAE, and H2OT.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, label processing, model configurations, training budgets, and evaluation procedures are identical. Both retain 5-fps inputs, 30-second sequences, three-second prediction, and 4–8-second interpolation gaps.

E4.justification: Table 3's component ablations, Appendix B's segment-length and hyperparameter analyses, qualitative examples, and the foot-camera constraint evaluation are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Experimental uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains A4Mer's 38.1% recognition-head accuracy and motion-prediction MPJPE of 150 mm on AMD and 120 mm on HiK.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, segmentation conditions, loss formulations, and the SMPL-fitting derivations in Appendix C are identical. No mathematical reasoning or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical movement representations, self-supervised A4Mer learning, AMD, and downstream benefits.

C2.justification: Interpretations of motion semantics and component behavior are unchanged, as are qualifications concerning HiK annotations, foot-camera localization failures, and mask-based annotation evaluation.

D1.justification: The first-page hyperlink changes from the laboratory homepage to a paper-specific address ending in /research/action-motifs/, providing more precise resource access guidance. Implementation and dataset documentation are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any new code or data release.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, dataset comparisons, novelty positioning, and cited works are identical.

P1.justification: Only the first-page URL text and arXiv version/date stamp change, from v1 dated 30 April 2026 to v2 dated 1 June 2026. Prose, terminology, headings, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The first-page URL and stamp updates do not reflow the document.

improvement.justification: Replacing the laboratory homepage link with a paper-specific project address provides a small improvement in resource access guidance. Scientific content, evidence, and appendix documentation are identical, so the benefit is limited to this more precise pointer; resource availability is not established by the PDFs.
